A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Look-Ahead Reasoning on Learning Platforms. Their complete main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and can be matched despite renumbering and rearrangement.

before.justification: v1 reports original credit-scoring simulations in Section 6, including convergence and collective-utility results, plus the feature-importance experiment in Appendix C.1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and their results in Figures 1–5, including the appendix experiment.

M1.justification: The level-k response recursion, collective optimization objective, population mixture models, and simulated manipulation strategies are unchanged. The appendix reformulation concerns mathematical documentation rather than a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GiveMeSomeCredit data and credit-scoring scenarios, covering mixed reasoning levels, feature manipulation, collective size, and target-model steering. No additional dataset or evaluation scenario appears.

E2.justification: The same selfish and collective strategy comparisons are retained. Appendix C.1 also retains the logistic-regression control trained without misreporting. Newly cited works are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C retain the same models, metrics, feature choices, and experimental settings, including epsilon = 0.5, the 0.01 learning rate with 250 epochs, and strategies optimized for collective sizes 0.3, 0.5, and 0.8.

E4.justification: The analyses varying reasoning mixtures, objective alignment, collective size, and manipulated features are unchanged. Appendix C.1 retains the same feature-importance experiment; no new ablation, robustness test, or case study is added.

E5.justification: Figure 1 continues to report standard deviations over 10 runs, and Appendix C.1 reports standard deviations over 10 train-test splits. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-reporting, or significance-testing change is documented.

E6.justification: Figures 1–5 retain the same plotted results, including convergence trends, alignment versus coordination benefit, collective-utility curves, and feature-importance bars. The corresponding empirical findings and result entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: The existing generalized bound, v1 Theorem 12 and v2 Theorem 5', now places the strategy derivative outside the expectation and explicitly parameterizes strategies. Its proof corrects the utility-gap expression. Section 5.1 also replaces positive definiteness and strict derivative signs with semidefiniteness and weak alignment signs. The principal results and proof approaches remain.

C1.justification: The abstract adds an explicit priority claim that the paper offers the first results characterizing coordination's utility trade-offs when contesting algorithmic systems. The central claims about convergence, unchanged selfish equilibria, and alignment-dependent coordination benefits are retained.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 expands the convex-loss interpretation and explicitly states that even size-aware optimal collective utility decreases with size in zero-sum games. The conclusion adds imperfect coordination as an unresolved extension. Existing simulation interpretations and the perfect-information limitation remain.

D1.justification: The implementation and dataset links, optimization settings, feature-centering description, manipulation construction, and target-model specification are unchanged. Appendix C contains no additional reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Levanon and Rosenfeld (2022), Kulynych et al. (2020), and Nestaas et al. (2025), extending connections to aligned incentives, protective optimization, and adversarial attacks. It also sharpens the novelty positioning relative to algorithmic collective action without substantially replacing the related-work discussion.

P1.justification: Localized edits revise the abstract, contributions, related work, collective-size discussion, and conclusion. Section 5.1 is renamed, and the generalized theorem and its proof are reorganized within Appendix A. The overall narrative and section structure remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The five numbered figures and Appendix B diagram are retained without changed graphical content. Figure 3's caption is lightly revised, while text reflow and spacing alter page composition and the positions of appendix graphics.

improvement.justification: The revised generalized-bound statement and proof reduce ambiguity in v1's strategy derivatives and utility-gap expression, while the expanded collective-size discussion and references improve exposition. These are limited gains with unchanged empirical support. A remaining caveat is that Section 5.1 now invokes a semidefinite Hessian while still using its inverse without addressing singular cases.
